transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
Lately I keep hearing this voice telling me my heart is going to give out and that it’s already too late for me. It sounds so clear and real, and I just don't know what to do anymore.
Along with hearing this voice, have you been feeling extremely sad, down, or hopeless lately?

Yes, I've been feeling this deep, dark emptiness almost constantly. It feels like a heavy weight is sitting right on my chest, and I just lie there thinking, "What's the point?" No matter what my wife says to comfort me, I just can't shake it.
Did you start hearing this voice only after you began feeling so deeply sad and empty, or was the voice already there before your mood changed?

The voice only started after I fell into this deep, dark sadness. Back when I was still working and singing in the choir, I never heard anything like that or believed my heart was doomed. It only began once I sank into this heavy spell where even getting out of bed felt impossible.
Have you recently started taking any new medications, or have you been using substances like alcohol or recreational drugs?
No, I don't drink alcohol or use any recreational drugs at all. I only take the medications that my doctors have prescribed for me, and I haven't started anything new recently.
Have you ever had a period of two weeks or more where your mood felt completely normal, but you still heard that voice or believed your heart was failing?

No, never. When my mood was normal, I never heard that voice or believed my heart was failing. It only started up after I sank into this deep, dark depression where I couldn't even find the strength to get out of bed.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or felt that life is no longer worth living?

Yes, I keep thinking it would be easier if my heart would just hurry up and quit, or if I helped it along somehow. I've sat alone in the garage more than once picturing different ways to make sure I don't wake up. I haven't actually tried to do anything yet, though.

Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt the exact opposite of this depression—such as having an unusual burst of energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling extremely high, wired, or irritable for several days in a row?

No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never had periods of feeling unusually high, wired, or having bursts of energy with little need for sleep. My mood has never gone to the opposite extreme like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe depressive episode characterized by persistent depressed mood, severe fatigue, loss of interest, and active suicidal ideation with planning. In addition, he experiences mood-congruent psychotic symptoms, including auditory hallucinations and somatic/nihilistic delusions (a voice telling him his heart is failing). These psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during the depressive episode, ruling out primary psychotic disorders like schizoaffective disorder (F25.1). The absence of manic or hypomanic history rules out bipolar disorder.
